explain.say: Milton refused rhyme, calling it a troublesome modern bondage. He wrote blank verse: unrhymed iambic pentameter, with sentences running on over line ends. Look at the first line's big word, broken into its beats. How does unrhymed verse change the feel?

explain.say: Here is the web of characters. Satan fathers Sin, Sin is mother of Death, and Satan tempts Eve. In Book Nine, Eve eats the fruit, and Adam eats it too, knowingly, because he cannot bear to lose her. Who carries more blame, and why?

explain.say: Is Satan the hero? On the left, Blake said Milton was of the Devil's party without knowing it. On the right, C. S. Lewis watched Satan shrink from archangel to snake, and Stanley Fish said the poem tests you, the reader. Superb. Challenge: track one Satan speech and decide.

faq.q: Why did Milton write Paradise Lost?
faq.a: He set out to tell the story of the Fall in the grandest form, a Christian epic to rival Homer and Virgil, and said his aim was to justify the ways of God to men.
asks: What was Milton's purpose in Paradise Lost?

faq.q: Is Satan the hero of Paradise Lost?
faq.a: Romantic poets like Blake and Shelley admired his defiance. Critics like C. S. Lewis argued he degenerates through the poem, and Stanley Fish argued the poem deliberately seduces readers to show their own fallenness.
Unrhymed iambic pentameter, ten-syllable lines of five beats without rhyme. Milton used it for Paradise Lost, as Shakespeare used it for much of his drama.

faq.q: Why does Adam eat the fruit?
faq.a: Not because he is deceived, as Eve is, but because he loves her and would rather fall with her than live without her. Milton presents this as both moving and wrong.
Milton was blind by 1652. He composed passages in his head, often at night, and dictated them to helpers, including his daughters and secretaries.
asks: Was Milton blind when he wrote Paradise Lost?

facts: Paradise Lost was first published in 1667 in ten books.
The second edition of 1674 rearranged the poem into twelve books.
